newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends slightly up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends slightly up in slow trading.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly up in slow trading on Monday with many investors staying on the sidelines due to the uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,690 yuan ($2,856) per tonne, rising 70 yuan.
It opened at 23,630 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 23,580 and a high of 23,700.
May fell 40 to 23,250, June rose 10 to 23,500, July 40 to 23,600, September 70 to 23,690 and October 60 to 23,580.
Combined volume fell to 20,900 tonnes from 31,570.
Copper opened little changed but speculative buying pushed prices up for most of the session with retail investors dominateing Monday's trading, traders said.
"Some speculative buying was responsible for today's rise while most investors stayed on the sidelines," one trader said. "A lack of market-moving news made copper move in a very narrow range today."
Physical prices are steady at around 23,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said they expected copper to move around the current level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down across the board.
May fell 20 to 15,280, June 90 to 15,550 and July 50 to 15,850.
Combined volume rose to 980 tonnes from 950.
